thurdock.notes: Thurdock's surface is a patchwork of humming root-hollows, black stone terraces, and walled market lands, all tinted by the cool grey light of a Grounded realm.
thurdock.summary: Thurdock is a world of grounded realms shaped by successive ages. Its story begins in the Singing, when the first roots condensed into soil and stone, with places like Mesium and Khurkurn still humming with that tone. The Seeding brought the makers, who planted the Weave across the fields, as at Osyuthis and Tarnardock. The Walled Age followed, with holding walls and guild orders, and then the Sundering and Shards tore old bonds apart; the Pact was sworn among survivors at places like Karouggar. The Holy Age saw temple orders keep sacred flames burning in towns such as Kalulanum and Brunar.

thurkok.name: Thurkok
thurkok.notes: Thurkok's grounded wastes of salt flats, ash and rust are rendered in dusty ochres and greys, with sparse green pockets where water is hidden.
thurkok.summary: Thurkok is a fictional omniverse of the Grounded realm, shaped by the Sundering, when worlds split and landfall broke old bonds. Its places range from salt basins and sunken fortresses to terraced grove-cities and walled court-cities, many marked by rusted hulks, causeways, and ruined pump-towers. Events include the Long Dimming, the Seeding that planted the Weave, the Singing that condensed the world's first roots, and the sealing of doors between worlds during the Courts. Caravan clans, toll-keepers, and scavenger brigades contest the wastes, while the first sovereign's groves and the Pact endure in scattered ruins.

toraizhoth.name: Toraizhoth
toraizhoth.notes: A hollow, humming world of reed terraces, basalt ridges and walled hill-towns, its soils ringing with the echo of the Singing and its skies moody with rain.
toraizhoth.summary: Toraizhoth is a world of terraced valleys, reed marshes, and walled towns shaped by the Singing and the Age of Sundering. Its places include Nestum, a hollow of pale reed-ground where the first roots of the world were gathered, and Brade, a basalt terrace split in the Sundering. Osuraneno is a walled town held by stone ramparts, and Joradolde a grove-city where the Courts gather. Its history includes Isivsethith, a rupture in the Age of the first sovereign, and Torougoth, a branching event of the Three Futures. Its records also cover martial standings, a recovery ward, and a sealed urban district used for covert missions.

crestardock.name: Crestardock
crestardock.notes: Grounded lowlands of salt, ash-scarred marsh and neon-lit ruin under a hazy amber-grey sky, with the Hollow soil's humming groves and Sundering-split cliffs.
crestardock.summary: Crestardock is a world of many settlements shaped by successive ages. Its story begins with the Singing, when roots condensed into the soil, and the Seeding, when makers planted the Weave. The Holy Age brought the Courts, walled hall-cities, and trials over the doors between worlds. The Age of Sundering followed, when landfall broke old bonds, split harbors and towns, and sealed ruined walls and bridges. Later eras left the Grounded realm of gaming halls, soundstages, and salt-cured terraces, while the Library shelves the branching Three Futures of its ending.

torourkoth.name: Torourkoth
torourkoth.notes: A sunken, humming world of salt flats, cisterns and hollow spires where tended valleys and drowned marshes sit under a grey, watchful sky.
torourkoth.summary: Torourkoth is a fictional world whose history runs from the Seeding, when the makers set the Weave into the soil and planted silver groves, through the Holy Age of temple fires and the Library of the Three Futures, to the Walled Age of fortified cities and orders, and the Fall, when the Sundering split the land and the Pact was sworn over its shards. Its places include terraced grove-towns, walled market cities, sunken salt-glass valleys, and river crossings. Recurring elements are temple flame, bells, groves, and walls. Events such as Crordath's Singing and the Sundering's landfall mark its ages.

tosistium.name: Tosistium
tosistium.notes: Tosistium's surface moves from the wet, humming root-groves and slow green lakes of the Seeding and Singing toward the dry, basalt-terraced badlands and walled market plains of the Sundering, with mild rain falling over the hollow soil.
tosistium.summary: Tosistium is a world shaped by the Singing, the Seeding, and the Sundering. Its first roots condensed from sound in undated soundings such as Amorus and Miiraemora, and the makers pressed the Weave into living soil in places like Thastasha and Ashyuzis. Walled city-states such as Serenollia, Cantum and Elemys grew up through the Walled Age, and landfall broke the old bonds during the Age of Sundering. The Library of Tosistium shelves the Three Futures, with lanterns such as Tarnardon and Nuirleth keeping branches of possibility alive.

voraikun.name: Voraikun
voraikun.notes: A grey ash-choked underworld of sealed hollows, flooded marshes and walled holdfasts, its surface tinted by dim lantern-light and drifting cinders.
voraikun.summary: Voraikun is a world of layered transit and ruin. Its rail network includes many underground stops and junctions, such as Cernolum, Oralisium, Viares and Terasor, where lines meet and transfer, alongside elevated routes like Vosus. Its settlements range from sunken harbor cities like Khoukoth and Vhozhak to walled market towns like Halonar and fortress-cities like Karouzhoth. The Weave and its sounding events shape the land, from Xaizith, when the first roots condensed out of the Singing, to Elionna, the quiet dormancy of the sleeping powers in the soil.

crestornen.name: Crestornen
crestornen.notes: A grounded, ash-laden world of dusty deserts, humming basalt ridges and drowned estuaries, its biomes drawn only from the surviving place entries.
crestornen.summary: Crestornen is a world of terraced court-cities, sheltered valleys, and drowned mountain-cities, where settlements like Lyennora, Silereth, Ilovaloma, and Tarnernath mark its history. Its records also hold many divergent timelines, time-travel branches, and tales of machine uprisings. Crestornen's chronicle reaches from the Seeding of its groves through the Age of Sundering, while countless alternate versions of its future remain in circulation.

crodaston.name: Crodaston
crodaston.notes: A grounded, drowned-tide world of salt marsh, reclaimed harbors, and ash-grey hills under a perpetual grey sky, with stone monuments and sunken cities standing above brackish water.
crodaston.summary: Crodaston is a planet of layered ages and ruined cities. Suramaneno, a terraced basalt valley, kept flame-shrines of the Holy Age through the Fall and Sundering, and Orianae was where the makers first set the Weave into the soil during the Seeding. Venireth marks the undated emergence of the world's first roots, and Venerys is a brief convergence where an age's possible endings are catalogued. Later districts such as Crustedon, Thaden, Moronudar, and Keluden show a grounded, fractured civilization of scavengers, markets, and sealed refuges, with wars like Drarnen and Pelurdeld shaping its history.

drernen.name: Drernen
drernen.notes: A grounded, humming world of rain-soaked valleys, fortified coasts, and sealed underground vaults, shaded by cool grey skies and marsh-dark forests.
drernen.summary: Drernen is a fictional world of grounded realms and drowned valleys. Its places include Bruldaron, a sunken terrace of lantern-lit canals where stilt-walkers tend reed gardens, and Fenesten, a terraced valley where temples of the Holy Age keep lamps burning. Moraron, a valley-city famed for rope-bridge markets, guards an old signal tower. Halurnedon is a drowned archipelago of basalt terraces whose Tidewright inhabitants once read the tides as scripture. Kelulde is a smoke-stained waystation where illicit cargoes and forbidden bargains are weighed. Keloste and Syezith add further settlements, with market towns, wells, and walled granaries.

drore.name: Drore
drore.notes: A grey, rain-soaked world of drowned cities, salt deserts and ash-grey reed basins, its dim violet-grey skies and quiet ruins shaped from the surviving Drore entries.
drore.summary: Drore is a fictional planet of delta cities, salt harbors, and highland basins, shaped by floods, tides, and old wars. Morurdon and Joradusteld are celebrated river and tidal market settlements, while Crorne serves as a capital of observatories and civic halls. Its history spans the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed out of the deep ground, the Seeding in the Weave, and the Sundering, when court-cities met to decide which doorways between worlds would stand. Tarnulden and Moranar hold sealed vaults and buried archives, and the Library of Drore records branching futures through events such as Silarlys and Elioneth.

drunesteld.name: Drunesteld
drunesteld.notes: A grey, rain-soaked world of drowned marsh-cities, basalt terraces and tide-bells, with dry rust-coloured ruins fading toward the desert edge.
drunesteld.summary: Drunesteld is a land of contested ground and drowned places. Its records describe Brastath, a crumbling fortress that witnessed conflict between the Iron Alliance and the Verdant Pact, and Moralden, a drowned orchard-city of salt-stained archives. Joruren is a drowned valley of black glass and rusted cranes, and Fenedane a tidal marsh-town of stilt markets. Halarnoron, a fortified valley town, has withstood repeated sieges. Thorar, a sunken valley-town, is known for tide-proof nets. Events include Jorenath, a short bitter uprising, and Thuldeld, a siege where engineers collapsed a granite keep with black powder.

kelarnock.name: Kelarnock
kelarnock.notes: A grey, dusk-lit world of basalt and glass where ash-dim skies, humming ruins and still dark water give way from frozen peaks through barren badlands to damp, sunless swamps.
kelarnock.summary: Kelarnock is a fictional world of the Outer realm, rendered in the entries as a place of drowned cities, drifting palaces, and recurring tidal events. Its sites include Crerduldon, a rust-colored basalt palace above a dead ocean, and Morerne, a drowned cathedral-city beneath a sunless sea. Recurring phenomena such as the Hollow Vigil at Crastoron and the tidal rite at Drustath recur across its reaches. Many locations hold memories, echoes, or altered time, and the world is marked by sealed vaults, silent waters, and lingering resonance.

osyuseth.name: Osyuseth
osyuseth.notes: A quiet, ash-touched world of ringing stone and hidden hollows, where a steaming jungle gives way to glassy badlands and frozen plains under a pale, dim sky.
osyuseth.summary: Osyuseth is a frontier world whose records blend many fragments. Thithora is a lush, sunken world with jungles and swamps over restless tectonics, and beneath its wastelands lies a stepped stone mountain with a sealed chamber. Xaastasha describes a cascade of sovereign uprisings in Osyuseth's outer drift-belts, where miners and haulers severed charter contracts and swore loyalty to a rival concord. Several entries address the wider reaches of this region but do not directly describe the planet itself.

shavseth.name: Shavseth
shavseth.notes: A violet-lit outer realm of drowned glass, frozen starlight, and slow ash-grey tides, with its driest ochre deserts and mist-wrapped basins fading toward cold crystal peaks.
shavseth.summary: Shavseth is an outer-realm planet of drifting shell-realms, drowned cities and reef-towers, its outer rings stretching across cosmic dust, glass seas and frozen lattices. Its places include Xaevsith, where Quiet Wardens keep orbits steady, Ashyuthis, a drowned shrine-city under green dusk, and Sheisora, a crystal reef-garden that endures collisions. Its events include Shistazith, a lock of six lattice-spires onto a plasma ring, and Xaethith, a silent unraveling by the Orrun Concord. Its defining quality is endurance across ages of orbit and tide.

theisasha.name: Theisasha
theisasha.notes: A scorched, ash-drifting surface of salt basins, glass-veined badlands and dim spore-forests, with frozen peaks and violet-tinged sky standing in for the quiet, dying-sun atmosphere of the entries.

xaatheth.name: Xaatheth
xaatheth.notes: A pale, humid, mist-wrapped world of ash-grey stone, hushed meadows and brackish seas, its biomes drawn from the sparse entries on the surface of Xaatheth.
xaatheth.summary: Xaatheth is a planet of drifting, strange realms and ruined megastructures. Entries describe Zephasis, a vast sunken corridor lit by one unbroken filament of cold white light, and Osesteth, an endless city of towers linked by sky-bridges. Other places include Xaissora, a realm of tidal dunes that exists only where sleeping minds press against the Outer veil, and Theshasora, a frozen highland under a perpetual violet dusk. Its outer reaches hold drowned sanctuaries, glass archipelagos, and sealed vaults. Ruined megastructures such as Taullontus and Tauntia stand among its landscapes, some linked to grander constructs and gestation engines.
